lines.text: Is it dangerous to charge your phone overnight?
You plug in your phone and go to sleep. Eight hours on the charger.
What most people picture is this: the battery fills up, the charger keeps pushing current, and it all ends up bursting.
That's a myth.
The charger isn't in charge. The phone is. Inside, a circuit watches the battery, and when the cell is full, it stops taking current.
The charger offers. Your phone decides.
But it sits there, pinned at a hundred percent all night. Every time it dips a little, it takes another sip.
And for a lithium battery, being full and warm is the worst thing there is. That's the real damage. It doesn't explode. It wears out.
That's why your phone has optimized charging. It parks at eighty percent and finishes the rest just before your alarm.
And the phones that blow up in the news? That does happen. But almost never because of the plug.
Inside the battery are two layers, kept apart by a paper-thin sheet. If something pierces it, the layers touch, and things spiral out of control in seconds.
What pierces it? A metal speck from the factory, or a hard knock. That's why phones also catch fire in pockets, not charging at all.
In a good cell, it's roughly one in ten million. And if the flaw comes from the factory, it's not your phone. It's the whole model.
The Galaxy Note 7 was pulled from the market: about two million phones in the US alone.
What is in your hands is this. It's not the time. It's where you leave it.
Under a pillow or between the sheets, the heat the battery gives off has nowhere to go. And heat is what turns an old or damaged battery into a fire.
And fake chargers. In a good one, a barrier separates the high voltage from the wall from the five volts that reach your hand. In fakes, that barrier barely exists.
Four hundred fake iPhone chargers were tested. Only three passed the insulation test.
An honest trick: weigh it. A charger that weighs nothing has nothing inside.
So, does it overcharge overnight? Myth. Does it shorten battery life? True. Can it catch fire? True, but it's extremely rare, and almost never from leaving it plugged in.
Sleep easy. Just get it out of the bed, and don't charge it with just anything.
